accent-dim.note: Defined in tokens but not yet consumed by a shipped component; reserved for a future secondary-alert tier.

paper-raised.note: Not yet consumed by any shipped component.

steel.note: Reserved for the masthead's double-rule border only.

display.purpose: The "POSTMORTEM" nameplate. Appears once, in the header.

headline.purpose: A bulletin's incident title. Deliberately not bold.

title.purpose: FLASH/URGENT/BULLETIN/ROUTINE — severity as typography, never color.

body.purpose: Meta lines: reporter, elapsed time, mitigation summary.

label.purpose: Short tracked-out uppercase micro-labels: subtitle, LIVE, status tags, claim button.

motion.name: pulse-ping
motion.purpose: The live-status dot's expanding ring, signaling an active/unresolved incident or the header's LIVE indicator.

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.purpose: The loading state's teletype cursor block, evoking a wire machine receiving copy.

components.name: Wire Header
components.description: The single persistent masthead: nameplate, subtitle, and a live heartbeat cluster (pulsing dot + LIVE + real-time UTC wire clock).
components.html:
POSTMORTEM

INCIDENT WIRE

LIVE15:53:05Z
components.css: @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } .ds-wire-header { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; padding: 16px 20px; border-bottom: 4px double var(--color-steel); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; } .ds-wire-header__nameplate { margin: 0; font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.01em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-wire-header__subtitle { margin: 2px 0 0; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.2em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-wire-header__live { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; padding-bottom: 2px; } .ds-wire-header__live-label { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.15em; color: var(--color-accent); } .ds-wire-header__clock { font-size: 14px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-pulse-dot { position: relative; display: inline-flex; height: 8px; width: 8px; } .ds-pulse-dot__ping { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-accent); opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-pulse-dot__core { position: relative; height: 8px; width: 8px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-accent); }

components.name: Precedence Stamp
components.description: Severity read through typography alone — weight, size, and tracking escalate from ROUTINE to FLASH. Never color.
components.css: .ds-precedence { font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-precedence--flash { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--urgent { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--bulletin { font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-ink); } .ds-precedence--routine { font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); }

components.name: Status Tag
components.description: The only place color signals urgency: live states pulse in Wire Red, resolved sits flat in Faded Wire Ink.
components.html: MITIGATED
components.css: @keyframes ds-ping { 75%, 100% { transform: scale(2); opacity: 0; } } .ds-status-tag { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-status-tag--live { color: var(--color-accent); } .ds-status-tag--resolved { color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-pulse-dot--sm { height: 6px; width: 6px; } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__ping, .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__core { height: 6px; width: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-accent); } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__ping { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0.6; animation: ds-ping 1.5s cubic-bezier(0,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-pulse-dot--sm .ds-pulse-dot__core { position: relative; }

components.name: Incident Bulletin
components.description: The feed row itself: no card shell, just a hairline bottom border, full-bleed against the page. Hovers to a flat tint, never a shadow.
components.html:
URGENT14:58Zauth-service

Elevated login latency after cert rotation

REPORTED BY T. ÁLVAREZ · 54M AGO
components.css: .ds-bulletin { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-rule); padding: 16px 20px; transition: background-color 0.15s; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-bulletin:hover { background-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-paper-dim) 60%, transparent); } .ds-bulletin__top { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-bulletin__meta { font-size: 12px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-bulletin__title { margin: 4px 0 8px; font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Mitigation Readout — Active
components.description: A live TTL countdown, recomputed every second against the real clock — read-time truth, not a cached push.
components.html: Pinned previous cert chain on edge nodesEXPIRES 58:51
components.css: .ds-mitigation { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-mitigation__summary { font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-ink-dim); } .ds-mitigation__expiry { margin-left: auto; flex-shrink: 0; font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink); }

components.name: Mitigation Readout — Expired
components.description: The alarm state: a solid Wire Red fill, the one other place besides the live-status dot where the reserved accent is spent.
components.css: .ds-mitigation-expired { display: flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-accent); background: var(--color-accent); padding: 6px 10px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--color-accent-ink); }

components.name: Claim Control — Unclaimed
components.description: The primary action: outlined at rest, fully inverts fill/text on hover and focus alike.
components.css: .ds-claim-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; min-height: 44px; padding: 0 16px; border: 1px solid var(--color-ink); background: transparent; color: var(--color-ink); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s, color 0.15s; } .ds-claim-btn:hover, .ds-claim-btn:focus-visible { background: var(--color-ink); color: var(--color-paper); }

components.name: Claim Control — Claimed
components.description: Once claimed, the control becomes a static stamp, not a toggle — ownership as a permanent mark, matching the audit trail's append-only discipline.
components.css: .ds-claimed-stamp { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; border: 1px solid var(--color-rule); padding: 4px 8px; font-family: 'Courier Prime', 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--color-ink-dim); }

narrative.overview:
PostMortem's dashboard is not a status-card grid — it's a continuous wire feed, the same discipline a newsroom telex applies to incoming copy: timestamped, precedence-graded, append-only, never silently edited. This is a deliberate refusal of the generic-SaaS dashboard default (colored status pills in a card grid); the system's own thesis is that the audit-trail discipline the product is built on — nothing is silently overwritten, every action punches a new line — deserves a visual form that behaves the same way. The page reads top-down like dispatch copy, most urgent and most recent first, not as a dashboard the eye has to hunt across.

The palette is near-monochrome by design: warm manila paper and dark ink by day, gunmetal ground and amber ink by night — the same machine under a different light source, not an inverted theme. A single hot accent, Wire Red, is spent almost nowhere, which is exactly why it reads instantly when it appears: the live/unresolved state, and the alarm when a mitigation's TTL has run out. Severity itself never touches color at all — FLASH/URGENT/BULLETIN/ROUTINE is a typographic ladder of weight and size, the wire service's own precedence vocabulary. Every surface is flat: no shadows, no rounded corners anywhere except the two functional live-pulse dots. Component feel is restrained and exacting — every stroke deliberate, nothing decorative, nothing added for warmth that isn't earned by function.
keyCharacteristics: Continuous append-only feed, not a card grid — one bulletin per incident, dividers not gutters.
Near-monochrome manila/gunmetal palette with exactly one reserved hot accent.
Severity communicated by typography (weight, size, tracking), never by color.
Zero shadows, zero border-radius except the two functional pulse dots.
Day desk / night desk: light and dark are two lighting conditions on one machine, not an inversion.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Wire Red appears in exactly two places: the live/unresolved status indicator and the expired-mitigation alarm. It is never used for hover states, severity, or emphasis of any other kind — if everything can turn red, nothing does.

rules.name: The Day Desk / Night Desk Rule
rules.body: Light and dark mode are not an inverted palette — they're two lighting conditions on the same machine (prefers-color-scheme, not a manual toggle). Every neutral and the accent both get an explicit day value and an explicit night value; neither is derived by inverting the other.

rules.name: The Precedence-By-Weight Rule
rules.body: Severity is FLASH / URGENT / BULLETIN / ROUTINE — words, never a color chip — and each step down the ladder loses weight, size, and tracking in the same motion. A reader triages by glancing at type density alone.

rules.name: The Flat Wire Rule
rules.body: No shadow, ever. If something needs to feel more important, it gets a heavier border or the one reserved accent color — never a drop shadow pretending the screen has depth it doesn't.

rules.name: The Right-Angle Rule
rules.body: Radius is reserved for exactly one thing: the circular pulse indicator that means "this is live." Every other shape in the system is a hard rectangle.

dos: Do reserve Wire Red exclusively for the live/unresolved status signal and the expired-mitigation alarm — nowhere else.
Do communicate severity through the Courier Prime weight/size/tracking ladder (FLASH → ROUTINE), never through a color chip.
Do give every color token an explicit day value and an explicit night value tied to prefers-color-scheme — never derive dark mode by inverting light mode.
Do keep every rectangular surface at 0 radius; the only permitted curve is the functional live-pulse dot.
Do set font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any live-updating numeral — clocks, countdowns, elapsed-time strings — so digits never jitter the layout.
Do keep interactive targets at a minimum 44px height, per the product's ICU-grade accessibility commitment.
donts: Don't add a second accent hue, a gradient, or a tinted shadow — the palette's entire force comes from staying near-monochrome with one reserved color.
Don't add box-shadow or simulated elevation anywhere; depth is stroke weight and tint delta only.
Don't round a button, card, or divider; radius is spent entirely on the two pulse-dot indicators.

Don't use the wire typeface (Courier Prime) for dense body or meta copy — it's reserved for the masthead, bulletin headlines, precedence stamps, and short control labels; long-running text stays in JetBrains Mono.
Don't turn "claimed" into a toggle a responder can undo casually — claiming is a stamp, a one-way mark, matching the audit trail's append-only discipline.
